# x86-64 corpus for llvm-mc.
#
# The integer instruction set is checked thoroughly against GNU as in
# tools/gas-diff; this corpus is mostly SIMD, where llvm-mc is the better
# oracle for AVX-512 decorators. The first block is a sanity check of the
# harness itself.
#
# --- covered extensions ---
#   MMX, 3DNow! and 3DNow!+ (including the suffix-byte opcode selector)
#   SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, AES-NI, PCLMULQDQ, POPCNT, LZCNT,
#   TZCNT, CRC32
#   AVX, AVX2 and FMA: two- and three-byte VEX, NDS/NDD operands, is4
#   selectors, VSIB gathers
#   AVX-512F with the VL forms of what it shares with AVX, plus the pieces of
#   BW and DQ that come for free with the same rows (vmovdqu8/16, vpaddb/w,
#   vpmullq, vandps): writemasks, {z}, {1toN} broadcast, embedded rounding and
#   {sae}, disp8*N at several tuple types, xmm16-xmm31 (R', V', X), EVEX VSIB
#   Opmask instructions: kmov, kand/kandn/kor/kxnor/kxor/kadd, knot, kortest,
#   ktest, kshift, kunpck
#   The rest of AVX-512 and the extensions after AVX2 are in x86-64-simd.txt,
#   x86-64-simd-intel.txt and i386-simd.txt, generated from GNU's opcode table.
#
# --- not covered ---
#   APX (REX2 / extended EVEX), AVX10.2, AVX-512 4FMAPS/4VNNIW
#
# --- deliberate divergences from llvm-mc ---
#   llvm-mc swaps the two sources of a commutative VEX instruction when that
#   moves an extended register into vvvv and so allows the two-byte prefix.
#   GNU as does not, and rsasm follows GNU as:
#     vaddps %xmm10, %xmm2, %xmm1   gas/rsasm: c4 c1 68 58 ca   llvm-mc: c5 a8 58 ca
#     vpaddd %xmm10, %xmm2, %xmm1   gas/rsasm: c4 c1 69 fe ca   llvm-mc: c5 a9 fe ca
#   Both assemblers agree on the non-commutative case, where the store opcode
#   of a move is used instead; that is covered below.
#
#   llvm-mc (22.1) misplaces a RIP-relative displacement followed by a 3DNow!
#   suffix byte: it measures from the start of the suffix rather than the end
#   of the instruction, so this addresses one byte past `data`:
#     pfadd data(%rip), %mm0 / ret / data: .quad 0
#       gas/rsasm: 0f 0f 05 01 00 00 00 9e    llvm-mc: 0f 0f 05 02 00 00 00 9e
#   objdump confirms the GNU as reading. tests/x86_simd.rs pins it instead.

nop
ret
movq %rbx, %rax
addq $1, %rax
movq 16(%rbx,%rcx,8), %rax
pushq %r12

# ---- MMX ----------------------------------------------------------------
paddb %mm1, %mm2

paddd %mm7, %mm0

movd (%rax), %mm0

# ---- AVX-512: register extension bits ---------------------------------------
vaddps %zmm1, %zmm2, %zmm3
# X is the fifth bit of a register-direct r/m, V' of vvvv, R' of reg.

vaddps %zmm1, %zmm2, %zmm19
vaddps %zmm25, %zmm26, %zmm27
vaddps %zmm9, %zmm10, %zmm11
vaddps %xmm16, %xmm1, %xmm2
vaddps %ymm16, %ymm17, %ymm18
vaddps (%r9,%r10,2), %zmm2, %zmm3
vmovaps %xmm17, %xmm1
vmovdqa32 %zmm17, %zmm2
vmovdqa32 %zmm9, %zmm2

# ---- AVX-512: writemasks, zeroing, rounding --------------------------------
vaddps %ymm1, %ymm2, %ymm3 {%k2}
vaddps %zmm1, %zmm2, %zmm3 {%k1}{z}
vaddps (%rax), %zmm2, %zmm3 {%k1}{z}
vmovups %zmm1, %zmm2 {%k1}{z}
vmovapd (%rax), %zmm1 {%k3}
vpaddq %zmm1, %zmm2, %zmm3 {%k1}
vaddps {rn-sae}, %zmm1, %zmm2, %zmm3
vaddps {rd-sae}, %zmm1, %zmm2, %zmm3
vaddps {ru-sae}, %zmm1, %zmm2, %zmm3
vaddps {rz-sae}, %zmm1, %zmm2, %zmm3
vaddss {rd-sae}, %xmm1, %xmm2, %xmm3
vsqrtps {rn-sae}, %zmm1, %zmm2
vcvtdq2ps {rn-sae}, %zmm1, %zmm2
# {sae} leaves L'L at zero rather than the vector length.
vmaxps {sae}, %zmm1, %zmm2, %zmm3
vminpd {sae}, %zmm1, %zmm2, %zmm3 {%k7}
vcmpps $0, {sae}, %zmm1, %zmm2, %k1
vcomiss {sae}, %xmm1, %xmm2
vcvttps2dq {sae}, %zmm1, %zmm2

# ---- AVX-512: broadcast and disp8*N ---------------------------------------
vaddpd (%rax){1to8}, %zmm2, %zmm3
vaddps (%rax){1to16}, %zmm2, %zmm3 {%k1}
vaddps (%rax){1to4}, %xmm2, %xmm3
vaddps (%rax){1to8}, %ymm2, %ymm3
vpaddd (%rax){1to16}, %zmm2, %zmm3
vpaddd (%rax){1to4}, %xmm2, %xmm3
vpaddq (%rax){1to8}, %zmm2, %zmm3
vxorpd (%rax){1to8}, %zmm2, %zmm3
vpternlogq $0x96, (%rax){1to8}, %zmm2, %zmm3
vpcmpq $1, (%rax){1to8}, %zmm2, %k3
vcmppd $1, (%rax){1to8}, %zmm2, %k1 {%k2}
vpsllq $3, (%rax){1to8}, %zmm2
vcvtdq2pd (%rax){1to8}, %zmm2
vcvtpd2ps (%rax){1to8}, %ymm2
# Full vector: N is the register width, or the element under broadcast.
vmovaps 64(%rax), %zmm0
vmovaps %zmm0, 64(%rax)
vaddps 64(%rax), %zmm2, %zmm3
vaddps 128(%rax), %zmm2, %zmm3
vaddps -64(%rax), %zmm2, %zmm3
vaddps -8192(%rax), %zmm2, %zmm3
vaddps 8128(%rax), %zmm2, %zmm3
vaddps 32(%rax), %ymm18, %ymm3
vaddps 16(%rax), %xmm18, %xmm3
vaddpd 8(%rax){1to8}, %zmm2, %zmm3
vaddps 4(%rax){1to16}, %zmm2, %zmm3
vpaddq 8(%rax){1to8}, %zmm2, %zmm3
# Not a multiple of N, or out of range once divided: back to disp32.
vaddps 4(%rax), %zmm2, %zmm3
vaddps -8256(%rax), %zmm2, %zmm3
vaddps 8192(%rax), %zmm2, %zmm3
vmovaps 64(%rax), %ymm0
# RIP-relative displacements are always 32 bits and never scaled.
vaddps 64(%rip), %zmm1, %zmm2
# Tuple1 scalar: N is the element, chosen by W.
vaddss 4(%rax), %xmm18, %xmm3
vaddsd 8(%rax), %xmm18, %xmm3
vaddsd 4(%rax), %xmm18, %xmm3
vcmpsd $1, 8(%rax), %xmm2, %k1
vmovsd 8(%rax), %xmm1 {%k1}
vmovq 8(%rax), %xmm17
vpbroadcastd 4(%rax), %zmm2
vpbroadcastq 8(%rax), %zmm2
vpbroadcastw 2(%rax), %zmm2
vbroadcastss 4(%rax), %zmm1
vbroadcastsd 8(%rax), %zmm1
# Full vector memory: never broadcast.
vmovdqu64 %zmm2, 64(%rax)
vpaddw 64(%rax), %zmm2, %zmm3
# Half vector: half the register.
vcvtps2pd 32(%rax), %zmm2
# Tuple4: a quarter of 512 bits, sized by W.
vbroadcastf32x4 16(%rax), %zmm1
vbroadcasti64x4 32(%rax), %zmm1
vinserti32x4 $1, 16(%rax), %zmm2, %zmm3
vinserti64x4 $1, 32(%rax), %zmm1, %zmm2
vextractf32x4 $1, %zmm1, 16(%rax)
vextracti64x4 $1, %zmm1, 32(%rax)
# Half, quarter and eighth memory: the vpmov* narrowings and widenings.
vpmovqd %zmm1, 32(%rax)
vpmovdb %zmm1, 16(%rax)
vpmovqb %zmm1, 8(%rax)
vpmovzxbd 16(%rax), %zmm2
vpmovsxwq 16(%rax), %zmm2
vpmovzxbq 8(%rax), %zmm2
# movddup reads one double at 128 bits, the whole register above.
vmovddup 8(%rax), %xmm17
vmovddup 64(%rax), %zmm1
vmovddup 32(%rax), %ymm1

# ---- AVX-512F: arithmetic and logic ---------------------------------------

vcmpss $1, %xmm1, %xmm2, %k1
vucomisd %xmm17, %xmm2
